correctness.rationale: An explicit GF(4) projective-plane representation has 21 point vectors, 21 line covectors and five elements per line; each two distinct lines intersect once. The finite dynamic programming identity W(S)=sum_{i in S: C(S-i) != C(S)} W(S-i) follows by deleting the final legal choice, with base W(empty)=1. Complete traversal of all 2^21 subsets excludes sets larger than ten and confirms precisely 140448 maximal supports, 36288000000 orders, 738840 reachable subsets and six profile populations. A separately coded forward dynamic program with independent field arithmetic gives identical figures. The explicit ten-step point sequence adds footprints 5,4,4,2,1,1,1,1,1,1, proving attainment. Bipartition separation gives total length 20 and binomial interleaving counts; degree-five covering lower bound and a whole-line cover give ordinary total domination 10.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact census on a classical 21-point Steiner design and its 42-vertex Levi graph, the first projective plane over a proper extension field. The gap between maximum legal sequences (10 per shore) and minimum covers (5 per shore), six support incidence profiles and exact counts for proper blocking versus line-containing supports are mathematically natural and not simply arbitrary parameter tuning. The sequence counts and independence product determine a reproducible, difficult extremal benchmark for order-dependent covering and total domination.
